title: The kingdom splits (1 Kings 12)
hookLine: Rehoboam ignores the elders' counsel, and ten tribes leave
last: ONE SMALL CHOICE AT A TIME.

cards: A new king, a crowd, and a request. Solomon has died. His son Rehoboam goes to Shechem, where all Israel has come to make him king.
Their spokesmen don't waste words: your father made our yoke heavy. Lighten the hard service and the heavy yoke, and we will serve you. Rehoboam says, go away for three days, then come back.
In those three days, he asks two groups for advice.

teach.h: THE ELDERS: BE A SERVANT THIS DAY.
teach.b: First he goes to the old men, in Hebrew the zekenim, the elders who had stood before his father Solomon.

Their advice, in the 1917 Jewish translation: "If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever."
Then he goes to the young men who grew up with him. They say the opposite. Tell them, my little finger is thicker than my father's loins.

teach.h: THE YOUNG MEN: WHIPS AND SCORPIONS.
teach.b: My father chastised you with whips; I will chastise you with scorpions. Rehoboam goes with the young men.
On the third day he gives the people the hard answer, and they cry back: "to your tents, O Israel; now see to thine own house, David."

The northern tribes walk away and make another man their king; only Judah stays with the house of David. A prophet had already spoken of ten tribes torn away; now it happens. Look at what the elders actually said.
Not be weak. Not give in on everything. Be a servant this day: one day of humility, for a lifetime of loyalty.
They had stood before Solomon and knew his reign from the inside. In this story the old counsel doesn't win because it's old.
It carries weight because it came from people who had seen a reign from start to finish.

teach.h: THEY WILL BE THY SERVANTS FOR EVER.
teach.b: Rehoboam had that advice in his hands, and he chose the voices that sounded like his own.

how: Jews read the division of the kingdom in the book of Kings; from here the story follows two kingdoms, Israel in the north and Judah, where David's house reigns.

o: the tribes that broke away to the north
elders: the old men who'd advised Solomon
the young men who grew up with the king

the cry as the tribes left

s: the elders told Rehoboam to give in on everything
they said to be a servant this day and speak good words, and the people would serve him for ever.
Rehoboam took three days before answering the people

games.q: you're the new king. the people ask you to lighten their load. the elders say serve them today; your friends say be harder than your father. what do you do?
games.why: Rehoboam followed the young men and answered roughly, and the people cried to your tents, O Israel, and the northern tribes left.

practice: Let the face of someone who has been at something longer than you come clearly to mind, a grandparent, a mentor, a neighbor.
What advice have they given you that you brushed aside, or what question could you ask them that you haven't yet? If you pray, you can ask to know good counsel when it comes.

wordCard.voice: Zekenim. The Hebrew word for elders, the ones Rehoboam heard out and then set aside. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: elders, old men. Rehoboam set aside the counsel of the zekenim.

carryVoice: Your line: heed the old counsel. The elders had seen the whole reign. See you tomorrow.
